title: Close a jaw coupling: spider into the fixed hub, loose hub turned to mesh and slid to its line
instruction: Couple the gear reducer to the driven shaft: the spider between the jaws of both hubs and the loose hub at the scribed line on its shaft.
context: Industrial machinery mechanics (O*NET 49-9041.00: "Repair or replace broken or malfunctioning components of machinery or equipment"; "Reassemble equipment after completion of inspections, testing, or repairs"; 446,900 US workers), machinery maintenance workers (49-9043.00: "Install, replace, or change machine parts and attachments, according to production specifications"; 59,700) and millwrights (49-9044.00; 40,700), 547,300 in all, renew the spider of the jaw couplings between drives and driven shafts: it is the coupling's wearing part. Unlike a printed coupling lowered over two unequal drive dogs (#192), aligning an already coupled shaft (#817), meshing a flexspline (#1890), keying a pulley onto a shaft (#2035, #2037) or a gear train (#893), here a six-legged spider goes between two three-jaw hubs, one of them on a shaft that turns when touched, the phase is found by contact, and the hub is slid to the catalogue spacing.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the bench (x forward, y left); both shafts lie along x on the line y 0, 9.0 cm above the bench; everything is bolted down except the spider. Coupling: Lovejoy L-100 jaw coupling, two sintered-iron hubs L100 x 5/8 in (64.5 mm across, 35.1 mm through the bore, three jaws 18.0 mm long, 0.70 kg each) and one L099/100 open-centre Hytrel spider (64.5 mm across its six legs, legs 10.9 mm thick, 26.2 mm centre hole, 15.5 mm wide, 27 g). Fixed side: a worm gear reducer (Boston Gear 713 size, cast housing 73 x 108 x 118 mm, 5.4 kg, 5/8 in output shaft that does not turn by hand) on a 31 mm steel riser, housing from x 45.7 to 53.0; its hub is set-screwed on the output shaft with its jaws toward the robot, jaw tips at x 39.2, one jaw straight up. Driven side: a 5/8 in steel shaft (218.5 mm long, 0.32 kg) from x 15.4 to 37.25 in two UCP202-10 pillow blocks (cast iron, centred at x 21.65 and 26.65) on a 60 mm steel base frame (88 x 140 mm); it turns freely (about 0.02 N m) and does not slide. Its end stands 19.5 mm from the fixed hub's jaw tips. The loose hub sits on this shaft's 3/16 in key, jaws toward the fixed hub, its rear face at x 31.55 (41.5 mm back from a line scribed round the shaft at x 35.7), turned 30 degrees from where its jaws would face the gaps between the fixed hub's jaws; it slides with about 1.4 N. Spider: standing on two leg tips in a wooden holder (60 x 80 mm board with two blocks 16.5 mm apart) at x 27, y -15, its faces square to x and two legs level, centre 3.7 cm above the bench.
scoring: End state, measured with a rule, feeler gauge and the trial video. 0.25: the spider sits between the fixed hub's jaws (its centre within 1.5 mm of the shafts' axis, within 5 degrees of square, its near face no more than 1 mm proud of the jaw tips) with the grippers at least 3 cm clear of it. 0.5: that, and the loose hub's jaw tips are 3 mm or more past the spider's near face, in its free gaps, with the grippers at least 3 cm clear of the loose hub and the driven shaft (a hub held in place earns nothing more). 0.75: that, and the loose hub's rear face is within 1 mm of the scribed line (its jaw tips then stand on the fixed hub's face, the catalogue spacing of 18.0 mm between the hubs). 1.0: that, with both grippers at least 3 cm clear of the spider, the loose hub and the driven shaft, and nothing moving for 1 second (in simulation no tracked point moves more than 1 mm; in a real trial no visible motion in the last second of the video). 0 in every other state, including the two hubs closed on each other with the spider left out. Which arm does what is not scored.
reset_notes: Slide the loose hub back until its rear face is 41.5 mm behind the scribed line (a pencil mark on the shaft) and turn the shaft until the hub's index mark is 30 degrees clockwise, seen from the robot, of the mark for meshing. Take the spider out and stand it in the holder's slot on two leg tips. Check that the fixed hub has one jaw straight up and its set screw is tight, that the loose hub slides under about 1.4 N (spring scale on its rim, along the shaft) and that the shaft turns under about 2.5 N at its surface (0.02 N m). Renew the spider if its legs are nicked.
fidelity: Full size, rigid, built from boxes; nothing is detected or scripted. The spider is rigid with 0.5 mm of play per side in the jaws (the real Hytrel one is a close fit); its leg edges carry a 0.6 mm facet for the moulded radius of about 1 mm. The hub slides on the shaft's key. Set screws are not modelled: the job stops at the catalogue spacing, before the screw is torqued (README). The demo video's close camera is for recording only: the policy's cameras, physics and scorer are unchanged.
